headline: UK Education Tech Firm Bromcom Suffers Single Sign-On Data Breach
title: Bromcom SSO Breach Exposes User Registration Data
summary: Bromcom, a UK-based software provider for educational institutions, has notified customers of a data breach affecting a legacy single sign-on (SSO) system. According to a report on October 7, 2026, an unauthorized party accessed and exfiltrated data including email addresses and registration details. Bromcom has assured customers that its core Management Information System (MIS) containing sensitive student data was not affected, and no passwords were compromised.
full_report:
## Executive Summary
**[Bromcom](https://bromcom.com/)**, a software provider for schools in the United Kingdom, has disclosed a data breach involving a legacy component of its single sign-on (SSO) technology. On October 7, 2026, it was reported that an unauthorized third party gained access to a server environment and exfiltrated user registration data. The compromised information includes email addresses and sign-in metadata. The company has emphasized that its core, more sensitive school Management Information System (MIS) was not impacted, and no passwords or authentication tokens were accessed. The incident highlights the persistent risk posed by legacy systems within an organization's infrastructure.

---

## Threat Overview
The breach was discovered by Bromcom on September 6, 2026, after users reported issues with SSO access. The investigation revealed that an attacker had gained unauthorized access to the company's Communication Server environment and retrieved data related to SSO registrations. In response, Bromcom has decommissioned the affected legacy system and engaged external forensic specialists to investigate the full scope of the incident. The company is now working with affected schools and regulatory authorities.

## Technical Analysis
The attack vector was the exploitation of a legacy system. While the exact method was not disclosed, this type of incident typically involves an unpatched vulnerability or a misconfiguration in an older, often overlooked, piece of infrastructure. This aligns with the MITRE ATT&CK technique [`T1190 - Exploit Public-Facing Application`](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/). The attacker's ability to access and retrieve data from the server also points to [`T1213 - Data from Information Repositories`](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1213). The incident underscores the importance of maintaining a complete asset inventory and having a clear lifecycle management plan for all systems, including decommissioning.

## Impact Assessment
The direct impact of the breach is limited, as Bromcom asserts that highly sensitive student data and passwords were not compromised. However, the exfiltration of email addresses and registration data is not without risk. This information can be used by threat actors to launch targeted phishing campaigns against school staff, students, and parents, using the context of their relationship with Bromcom to make the scams more convincing. The incident also carries reputational damage for Bromcom within the education sector.

## IOCs — Directly from Articles
No specific Indicators of Compromise were provided in the source articles.

## Cyber Observables — Hunting Hints
To find risks associated with legacy systems, organizations can hunt for:
| Type | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| other | (Out-of-support software versions) | Use asset inventory and vulnerability scanners to identify any systems running software that is past its end-of-life (EOL) date. |
| other | (Systems with no owner) | Identify servers or applications within the environment that do not have a clearly documented business or system owner. |
| network_traffic_pattern | (Traffic to/from legacy systems) | Analyze network traffic to and from known legacy systems to ensure it aligns with expected behavior. |

## Detection & Response
- **Asset Inventory:** Maintain a comprehensive and up-to-date asset inventory that includes all hardware and software, their versions, and their operational status (e.g., production, staging, legacy). This is a foundational step in D3FEND's [`Platform Hardening`](https://d3fend.mitre.org/technique/d3f:PlatformHardening).
- **Log Monitoring:** Ensure that all systems, including legacy ones, are sending logs to a central SIEM. Monitor these logs for any signs of anomalous access or activity.
- **Decommissioning Process:** When a legacy system is decommissioned, ensure that it is fully removed from the network, all associated data is securely archived or destroyed, and any related firewall rules are removed.

## Mitigation
- **Lifecycle Management:** Establish a formal technology lifecycle management policy. This policy should define the process for retiring and replacing old systems before they become an unacceptable security risk.
- **Network Segmentation:** Isolate legacy systems that cannot be immediately decommissioned. Place them in a separate network segment with strict access controls and enhanced monitoring to limit their potential impact on the rest of the environment. This aligns with D3FEND's [`Network Isolation`](https://d3fend.mitre.org/technique/d3f:NetworkIsolation).
- **Vulnerability Management:** Even if a system is designated as 'legacy,' it must remain part of the vulnerability management program. If patches are not available, compensating controls must be implemented to mitigate known risks.

d3fend_countermeasures.recommendation: The Bromcom breach underscores the importance of Platform Hardening, specifically through robust asset and lifecycle management. Organizations must maintain a complete, accurate inventory of all hardware and software assets, including their age, owner, and support status. For legacy systems like the compromised SSO component, a clear end-of-life (EOL) plan is essential. This involves not just turning the system off, but also ensuring all associated firewall rules are removed, DNS records are deleted, and data is securely archived or destroyed. By proactively identifying and retiring these high-risk legacy assets, organizations can eliminate entire classes of vulnerabilities before they can be exploited.

cyber_observables.description: Identifying systems running unsupported or EOL software is a key indicator of risk from legacy systems that may contain unpatchable vulnerabilities.
